transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I can't stop fixating on how bad I look in every picture, and it's starting to really interfere with my work and social life. It has gotten so overwhelming lately that I felt like I finally needed to talk to someone about it.
Can you tell me more about what specifically bothers you about your appearance in pictures, and do you find yourself repeatedly checking or trying to fix these perceived flaws?

In photos, all I can see is how huge and crooked my nose looks and how uneven my skin is, and I'll zoom in and pick myself apart for hours. To try and fix it, I take dozens of selfies to check my angles, redo my makeup over and over, and constantly ask my mom or roommate if I look weird. I even end up changing my outfits three or four times before work because I'm just so self-conscious.
Do you find yourself performing any specific rituals or compulsions, such as excessive cleaning, checking, or arranging, beyond just your appearance-related concerns?

No, I don't experience those types of rituals or compulsions at all. My focus is entirely on how my face and clothes look, and I don't have any habits like excessive cleaning or arranging outside of that.

Can you tell me if your excessive concern about your appearance is primarily driven by a fear of being judged or evaluated by others, or is it more about your own personal dissatisfaction with how you look?

It really feels like a combination of both. I have this intense personal dissatisfaction where all I can see is my crooked nose and uneven skin, but I also get terrified of how others judge me, especially when coworkers tag me in photos or when I'm visible at work events.
Can you estimate how much of your distress is due to your own negative self-image versus the fear of what others might think of your appearance?

It’s really hard to separate them because they are so deeply intertwined, but it starts with my own disgust when I look at my huge, crooked nose and uneven skin. However, the fear of other people seeing those flaws is just as massive, which is why I dread being tagged in photos by coworkers and constantly ask my mom and roommate for reassurance.
Have you ever experienced recurring, intrusive thoughts or urges that are not related to your appearance, such as fears of contamination, harm to others, or needing things to be symmetrical?
No, I don't experience those kinds of thoughts or urges at all. My focus is strictly on my appearance and how bad I look, rather than things like contamination or symmetry.

Can you describe how you would feel and what you would do if you were in a situation where you couldn't check your appearance for an extended period, such as being in a meeting or on a trip without access to mirrors or photos of yourself?

I would feel incredibly anxious and panicked, completely distracted by the constant worry that my nose looks huge and crooked or that my skin looks terrible. To cope, I'd probably try to sneakily use my phone screen to check my angles, repeatedly ask someone for reassurance, or just try to escape the situation entirely. It would be almost impossible for me to focus on anything else.
Do you find that your preoccupation with your appearance significantly interferes with your daily functioning and relationships, to the point where it's hard to think about or focus on anything else?

Yes, it definitely does. I've started turning down presentations, rearranging event schedules to avoid cameras, and my supervisor even confronted me about being late and unreliable. I've also been backing out of community activities, and my friends and parents are really worried because they barely see me anymore.

Can you tell me if there are any times or situations where your obsessive thoughts about your appearance are replaced by or co-occur with other obsessive thoughts or compulsions that are not related to your appearance?

No, I don't really experience other types of obsessive thoughts or compulsions that are unrelated to how I look. My worries and habits are almost entirely focused on my physical appearance and how I look in photos.

Can you describe if your repetitive behaviors, such as taking dozens of selfies or repeatedly checking your appearance, are aimed at preventing some dreaded outcome or reducing anxiety related to your appearance, or are they purely driven by your dissatisfaction with how you look?

It’s a mix of both, but it is heavily driven by intense anxiety and the urge to prevent looking "weird" or "terrible" to others. I take selfies to check my angles and constantly redo my makeup or change outfits to try and hide my nose and skin before anyone else can see me. I also ask my mom and roommate for reassurance because I am constantly anxious and want to avoid the absolute dread of ending up in a photo where my flaws are visible.

When you're having these intrusive thoughts about your appearance, do you feel like you're unable to control them or that they're interfering with your ability to think about other things, similar to how someone might feel if they were having obsessive thoughts about contamination or harm?

Yes, I feel completely unable to control those thoughts once they start. As soon as I see a photo or start thinking about my nose or skin, it completely takes over my mind and I'll spend hours picking apart my flaws. It makes it absolutely impossible to focus on anything else.

Can you think of any situation or trigger that could lead you to have obsessive thoughts or compulsions that are completely unrelated to your appearance, or are your obsessive thoughts and compulsions exclusively focused on how you look?

No, my obsessive thoughts and behaviors are completely and exclusively focused on how I look, especially my nose and skin in photos. I don't have any thoughts or compulsions like this about anything unrelated to my appearance. It really is strictly about my physical looks.

Can you describe if there's ever a time when your obsessive thoughts about your appearance feel more like a fear of a specific, catastrophic outcome, such as being rejected by others due to your looks, rather than just a general dissatisfaction with how you look?

I haven't really thought about it in terms of a fear of rejection. Instead, I'm just completely overwhelmed by how awful I think I look, especially my nose and skin. The urge to hide from cameras and avoid being seen comes from a deep dissatisfaction and embarrassment about my appearance, rather than a conscious fear of people rejecting me.

Can you imagine a scenario where you would be completely satisfied with your appearance, but still experience significant distress or anxiety due to other obsessive thoughts or compulsions unrelated to how you look?

I'm not really sure about that, and I haven't really thought about it. Right now, my anxiety and distress are completely tied to how I look and my appearance in photos, so it's really hard to imagine experiencing obsessive thoughts about anything else.

If you were to somehow magically wake up tomorrow and feel completely satisfied with your appearance, do you think you would still experience any obsessive thoughts or compulsive behaviors, or would all of your distress and anxiety completely disappear?

If I woke up tomorrow completely happy with my appearance, I honestly believe all of my anxiety and distress would completely disappear. All of my checking behaviors and avoidance are entirely driven by how unhappy I am with my nose and skin. If I felt good about how I looked, I wouldn't have any reason to hide from cameras or obsess over photos.

If you were able to completely accept and feel satisfied with your appearance, do you think you would still have obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other things, or would your obsessive thoughts and compulsions completely go away?
I'm not really sure about that. I've only ever focused on my appearance, so I haven't really thought about whether those kinds of thoughts would show up in other areas of my life.

If you were able to completely overcome your concerns about your appearance, do you think you might develop obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other aspects of your life, or do you believe your obsessive thinking pattern would completely resolve?

I'm really not sure about that, as I haven't thought about whether my obsessive thinking would shift to other things. Right now, I am just so completely consumed by my worries about my appearance that I can't even imagine focusing on anything else.

If you were to experience a significant reduction in your obsessive thoughts about your appearance, do you think you would then start to worry excessively about other aspects of your life, such as work, relationships, or health, or would your overall level of obsessive thinking decrease?

I'm really not sure and I haven't really thought about that. Right now, my mind is so completely consumed by how I look in photos and my appearance that I can't even imagine what it would be like to not worry about it, let alone if those worries would shift to something else.

Can you think of any situation where your obsessive thoughts might shift from your appearance to another area of your life, such as work or relationships, if your appearance concerns were somehow resolved?

I haven't really thought about that and it's hard to imagine. My worries about my appearance are so overwhelming right now that I can't even picture what it would be like to have them resolved, let alone if they shifted to something else like work or relationships.

If your appearance concerns were completely resolved, do you think you would still experience obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other aspects of your life, such as work, relationships, or health?

I'm really not sure and I haven't thought about it. Currently, all of my worries and repetitive behaviors are entirely focused on my appearance and how I look in photos, so it's hard to imagine my mind shifting to anything else.
If your concerns about your appearance were to completely disappear, do you think you would still experience obsessive thoughts or compulsions, but about something other than your appearance?

I'm really not sure and I haven't thought about that. My worries and habits have always been entirely focused on my appearance—specifically my nose and skin—so it's hard to imagine obsessing over anything else.

Do you think your obsessive thoughts and compulsions about your appearance are similar in nature to the obsessive thoughts and compulsions experienced by someone with obsessive-compulsive disorder, such as excessive cleaning or checking, or are they distinctly different because they are focused on your appearance?
I'm not really sure and I haven't really thought about it that way. I just know that all of my own worries and habits are completely focused on how I look in photos and my appearance.

If you were to experience a significant reduction in your obsessive thoughts about your appearance, do you think you would then start to worry excessively about other aspects of your life, such as work, relationships, or health, or would your overall level of obsessive thinking decrease?
I'm really not sure and I haven't thought about what would happen if these worries stopped. I don't know if my anxiety would shift to other things like work or health, or if it would just go away.

If you were completely satisfied with your appearance, do you think you would still experience obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other things, such as contamination, symmetry, or harm, like someone with obsessive-compulsive disorder might?

I don't really experience those kinds of thoughts or compulsions about things like contamination or harm. My worries are almost entirely focused on my appearance, so I don't think I would have those other concerns.
Do you think your obsessive thoughts about your appearance are ego-dystonic, meaning they feel alien or unwanted, or are they more aligned with your own self-criticism and negative self-image?

I'm not really sure how to categorize it in those terms, to be honest. I just genuinely believe that I look terrible in photos and I can't stop focusing on it, rather than trying to analyze if the thoughts feel alien or aligned with my self-image.

If you were to experience a significant reduction in your obsessive thoughts about your appearance, do you think you would still have the tendency to develop obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other aspects of your life, or would your overall pattern of obsessive thinking completely change?

I'm really not sure about that, and I haven't thought about it. I'm just so consumed by how terrible I look in pictures right now that I can't even imagine what my thoughts would be like if that worry went away.

If you were to somehow overcome your obsessive thoughts about your appearance, do you think you would still experience obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other things, or would they completely disappear?
I'm really not sure and I haven't thought about that. My focus has been entirely on my appearance lately, so it's hard to say if I would have obsessive thoughts about other things if that went away.

If you were to overcome your obsessive thoughts about your appearance, do you think you would still experience obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other aspects of your life, such as contamination, symmetry, or harm, which are common in obsessive-compulsive disorder?

I haven't really experienced thoughts or compulsions about things like contamination, symmetry, or harm. My anxiety and habits have been entirely focused on my appearance and how bad I look in photos. It's really hard to imagine my mind shifting to those other kinds of worries.
If you were to wake up tomorrow with no concerns about your appearance, do you think you would still have obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other things, such as cleanliness, order, or safety?
No, I don't really experience obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other things like cleanliness, order, or safety. My worries are really just focused on how I look.

If you were to somehow overcome your obsessive thoughts about your appearance, do you think you would still experience obsessive thoughts or compulsions about other aspects of your life, such as work, relationships, or health, or would your overall level of obsessive thinking decrease?

I'm really not sure and I haven't thought about that. My mind is just so completely consumed by my appearance concerns right now that I can't even begin to imagine how my thinking would change if they were gone.
